Before I say I’m sorry, there’s a story I want us to revisit. Not to erase what happened, and not to ask you to forget. Just to remember what we built, and to be honest about what I hope we could build again.

Take your time. There’s no rush.

03 / THE PART I OWN

I know I hurt you.
I won’t dress it up.

An apology should be honest before it tries to be beautiful.

We faced people who doubted us, pressure, arguments, silly fights, and genuinely difficult days. You stood beside me when I struggled with my exams, and you stayed until I got through them. We graduated together. I came to meet your mum, and that step meant a lot to me.

Then things got difficult, and I chose to walk away. I know that leaving you like that was wrong. Later, I got involved with someone else, and I understand that this may have hurt you and made it harder to trust what I say now. I won’t use my feelings as an excuse or ask you to ignore the impact.

I can’t change what happened. I can only own my part, listen to what it was like for you, and show—over time—that I can do better.

I’m sorry for the hurt I caused. You deserved honesty, care, and consistency.

05 / THE LETTER I OWE YOU

What I wish I had said
with more care.

To someone who still means so much to me,

I’m not making this to pull you back into the past or pretend everything was perfect. I’m making it because I remember.

I remember the Faculty of Archaeology, sitting around Faculty of Arts, Ramadan breakfasts at McDonald’s, our university days, the TikToks, the photos, the videos, the ridiculous arguments, and the difficult ones. I remember you standing beside me when I needed it. I remember graduating together and how much it meant to me to meet your mum.

I remember the good, but I’m not forgetting the ways I hurt you. I chose distance when I should have faced things more honestly. And I know that getting involved with someone else could have damaged your trust in me. I’m sorry.

I still care about you deeply. You have a special place in my heart, and if there is even a small part of you that wants to see whether we can try again, I would be grateful for that chance. Not because our history obliges you to come back, but because I believe we could build something healthier if we both genuinely want to.

I’m not asking you to forget, decide today, or trust me before I’ve earned it. I want to start with honest conversations, small steps, and actions that match my words. I would rather rebuild slowly and truthfully than promise you the world and let you down again.

If you don’t feel ready, I will respect that too. Your feelings matter, and you deserve the space to make your own choice.

I’m sorry. I still have hope for us—but I want any new beginning to be something we both choose.

— From my heart
06 / SOMETHING JUST FOR US

Can I treat you
to a little time together?

No big label, no pressure, and no expectation. Just a chance to sit, talk, laugh, or do something different. You get to choose what feels comfortable.

First, choose a day that works for you.

Pick any date you like. We can change it together if plans don’t work.

Then, choose what you’d enjoy.

This choice stays on this page. It does not send a message or book anything. You can show me your choice or we can decide together—only if you want to.

07 / NO PRESSURE

You don’t have to
answer everything today.

This isn’t a decision you owe me. It’s just a little space for what feels right to you.

These are just interactive words on this page. Nothing is sent anywhere.

ONE LAST THING
I don’t just miss the memories.
I hope we can make better ones.

I can’t ask the past to fix the present. I can only be honest about what you mean to me, take responsibility for my mistakes, and hope that—if you want it too—we might find a new beginning, one small step at a time.

No promise demanded. Just a sincere hope, and room for your choice.
A real story. An honest apology. No perfect promises.
Take your time.
